q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me analyze this step-by-step.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-15. Q2 FY2027 earnings would typically be released around August 2026 for the quarter ending July 2026. Given that we're already at mid-August 2026, this earnings release may have already occurred or is imminent. The research indicates that Q1 FY2027 earnings were released on May 20, 2026. Q2 FY2027 would typically be released about 3 months later (late August 2026). So roughly **2-4 weeks** remain until resolution.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research provides NVIDIA's **Q1 FY2027 guidance of $91.0 billion ± 2%** (range: $89.18B to $92.82B), released May 20, 2026. This guidance is described as NOT assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China.

For Q2 FY2027 (the quarter we're forecasting), I need to consider:
- NVIDIA's historical sequential growth patterns
- The stated guidance already provided for Q2 FY2027 in the research
- Current macro environment and demand trends

The research states this Q1 guidance "does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China" - this suggests uncertainty about China revenue that could affect Q2 guidance.

**Key insight**: The research explicitly states "NVIDIA's forward guidance for its Q2 FY2027 earnings, released on May 20, 2026, projects revenue of **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**."

This appears to be the actual Q2 FY2027 guidance that was provided. The $91.0B ± 2% translates to a range of $89.18B to $92.82B.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Actual Data Center demand weaker than expected
- China revenue restrictions tightening further
- Macro slowdown impacting enterprise capex
- Execution issues or supply chain problems
- Competition intensifying in GPU market
- The ± 2% guidance band could resolve at the lower end

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected AI/Data Center demand
- China revenue materializing despite restrictions
- Higher margin products driving more revenue
- Cloud providers accelerating capex beyond current plans
- Better-than-expected execution
- The ± 2% guidance band could resolve at the upper end or NVIDIA beats guidance

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides NVIDIA's own stated forward guidance for Q2 FY2027: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**. This is the most direct and reliable data point available.

---

## Analysis

The research explicitly contains NVIDIA's actual Q2 FY2027 forward guidance already issued on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (range $89.18B to $92.82B).

Since this is forward guidance that has already been issued, the question is asking what value will actually be guided/provided. The guidance is already in the public record at $91.0B ± 2%.

NVIDIA typically guides conservatively and beats their own guidance. The ± 2% band allows for $89.18B to $92.82B. Given:
- NVIDIA's historical tendency to provide achievable guidance and beat it
- The midpoint guidance of $91.0B is already $4.16B above the LSEG consensus of $86.84B
- The uncertainty around China revenue could push either direction
- We're at the resolution date (August 2026), very close to when Q2 earnings would be reported

The most likely outcome is that the actual Q2 FY2027 revenue guidance announced will be at or near the $91.0B midpoint, with reasonable probability of beating it slightly within the guidance range or potentially modestly above.

Given the guidance range of $89.18B to $92.82B is already publicly stated, and considering NVIDIA's track record of meeting or beating guidance, I expect the actual reported guidance to cluster around $91.0B with some upside potential.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for its Q2 FY2027 earnings, released on May 20, 2026, projects revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). This guidance does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

The company also expects GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins to be 74.9% and 75.0%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are anticipated to be approximately $8.5 billion and $8.3 billion, respectively [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). For the full fiscal year 2027, NVIDIA projects GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates between 16.0% and 18.0% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance is higher than the LSEG average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).
